obligations.summary: A market surveillance authority may authorise, for a limited period and upon duly justified request, the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets, while conformity assessment procedures are completed without undue delay.
exceptions: Authorisation is only a temporary derogation from Article 43 while conformity assessment is being carried out.
For high-risk AI systems related to products under Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A, only the derogations established in that legislation apply.

obligations.summary: Law-enforcement or civil protection authorities may put a high-risk AI system into service without prior authorisation in duly justified urgent situations involving exceptional public security or imminent threat to life or physical safety, provided authorisation is requested during or after use without undue delay, and if authorisation is refused, use must be stopped immediately and all results and outputs discarded.
exceptions: Urgency and imminent threat to life or physical safety justifies use prior to obtaining authorisation, provided authorisation is sought without undue delay.
If authorisation is refused, use must cease immediately and all outputs must be discarded.

obligations.summary: A market surveillance authority shall issue an authorisation under paragraph 1 only if it concludes that the high-risk AI system complies with the requirements of Section 2 of Chapter III.

The market surveillance authority that issues an authorisation pursuant to paragraphs 1 or 2 shall inform the Commission and all other Member States of that authorisation, except where sensitive operational data relating to law-enforcement activities is concerned.
exceptions: This notification obligation does not cover sensitive operational data in relation to the activities of law-enforcement authorities.

obligations.summary: Where no objection is raised by a Member State or the Commission within 15 calendar days of receipt of the notification of an authorisation, that authorisation shall be deemed justified.

Where objections are raised by a Member State or the Commission within 15 calendar days of notification, the Commission shall without delay enter into consultations with the relevant Member State, consult the operators concerned and allow them to present their views, and then decide whether the authorisation is justified.
Where the Commission considers an authorisation unjustified, the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned shall withdraw it.

For high-risk AI systems related to products covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A, only the derogations from the conformity assessment procedure established in that Union harmonisation legislation shall apply.
exceptions: The general derogation mechanism under this article does not apply to products covered by Annex I Section A Union harmonisation legislation; only those specific legislative derogations apply.
